**This is the last release you install with a cable.** From here on the board updates itself: pick your WiFi, type the password once, tap INSTALL.

**Install this one over USB like every release so far.** v1.7.1 has no update code in it, so it cannot take an update over the air. Your settings, PIN and mesh pairings stay put.

## Updates over WiFi

Settings → SYSTEM → UPDATE FIRMWARE → UPDATE OVER WIFI. The board lists the networks it can see, you type the password on a new keyboard with capitals and symbols, and it downloads the latest version for your exact board straight from squachwatch.com. No computer, no browser, so it works for iPhone owners too.

Detection and Bluetooth switch off while it downloads to make room, and the board restarts at the end.

## Nothing gets in that shouldn't

Every update is signed, and the board refuses anything that isn't signed by this project or wasn't built for its own board, so a wrong screen driver can't sneak on as a white screen.

A new version starts on trial. If it crashes or loses power in its first 30 seconds, the board goes back to the version it had.

The saved WiFi password is erased by the duress PIN along with your other secrets.

## Switch back

The version you were running stays in the other slot. SWITCH TO puts you back on it in a few seconds, with no download and no WiFi.

## Updates over Bluetooth (beta)

The same update can also be sent from squachwatch.com/update in Chrome or Edge on a computer, or Chrome on Android. It is marked beta because it has not been tested on enough computers and phones yet. If it stalls, nothing on the board changes. iPhone browsers can't use Bluetooth; use WiFi.

## RL Phantom 2.4"

The RL Phantom is in the flasher's board list. This is the resistive-touch version (the part number ends in R). Touch now follows the screen when you rotate it, and a new board runs touch calibration on its first start.

## Also

Diagnostics shows which firmware slot is running and what is in the other one. Installing from the website now always takes effect, even on a board that has updated over the air. The flasher's version list no longer calls the newest release "master".

### The actually-useful part
- **Added**: firmware updates over WiFi, straight from squachwatch.com
- **Added**: firmware updates over Bluetooth from squachwatch.com/update (beta)
- **Added**: SWITCH TO, to go back to the version in the other slot
- **Added**: a WiFi password keyboard with capitals and symbols
- **Added**: signed updates, checked against the board they were built for
- **Added**: a 30-second trial for new versions, with automatic rollback
- **Added**: RL Phantom 2.4" (resistive) in the flasher's board list
- **Added**: firmware slot information on the diagnostics screen
- **Changed**: RL Phantom touch follows screen rotation and calibrates on first start
- **Changed**: the duress PIN also erases the saved WiFi password
- **Fixed**: a website install could be ignored by a board that had updated over the air
- **Fixed**: the flasher's version list labelled the newest release "master"
